subtopics.title: Site, Situation and the Rural World

questions.question: The cleanest statement of the difference between site and situation is:
options: Site is the actual ground a settlement occupies; situation is its position relative to rivers, routes and other places
Site is the settlement's position among its neighbours; situation is the ground it stands on
Site applies to villages only and situation to cities only
The two terms are interchangeable in mapwork

questions.question: A rural settlement whose houses gather closely around a single shared borehole shows which pattern?
Which of the following is a PUSH factor in rural-urban migration?
The leg of land reform that returns land to people dispossessed after nineteen thirteen is:

subtopics.title: Urban Settlements — Hierarchy, Structure and Issues

questions.question: Urbanisation is defined as:
options: The uncontrolled outward spread of a city
A rising percentage of a population living in urban areas
The absolute growth of a city's population
The drift of people from cities to small towns

questions.question: A specialist heart hospital counts as a high-order service because it:
options: Needs a very large threshold population and draws people from a large range
Has the smallest sphere of influence

questions.question: In the South African city model, townships and informal settlements typically stand:
options: On the far periphery, behind deliberately planned buffer strips of open land

questions.question: Urban blight collects most visibly in:
options: The transition zone of aging factories and flats around the core

subtopics.title: Economic Geography — Sectors, Farms, Mines and Factories

questions.question: Fishing, car assembly, banking and university research belong, in order, to which sectors?
Although agriculture contributes only a few percent of gross domestic product, it is considered vital because it:
options: Is the largest sector in the account books
Anchors food security, exports and rural employment

questions.question: Which list names the four core industrial regions as a set?
options: Gauteng (PWV), Durban-Pinetown, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage, South-western Cape
Coega, Richards Bay, Saldanha, East London

questions.question: The difference between an Industrial Development Zone and a Spatial Development Initiative is that:
options: A zone is a farming scheme while a corridor is a mine
The two names describe the same policy
A zone lies inland while a corridor runs only along the coast
A zone is a purpose-built industrial estate tied to a port; a corridor is a line of coordinated investment linking regions

subtopics.title: The Mapwork Toolkit — Calculations, Interpretation and GIS

questions.question: On a 1:50 000 topographic map, one centimetre on the map represents:
options: Half a kilometre on the ground

questions.question: Average gradient is calculated as:
options: Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent, expressed as a ratio like 1:25
Horizontal equivalent divided by vertical interval
Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale
Map distance multiplied by the scale

questions.question: Compared with the 1:50 000 topographic map, the 1:10 000 orthophoto map is:
options: The same scale, printed in colour
Five times larger in scale, showing photographic detail with contours overlaid

questions.question: In GIS, drawing a zone of stated width around a river to test which features fall inside it is called:

subtopics.title: The Village, the Taxi and the City

questions.question: In the story, the village general dealer closes after many residents leave because the shop has lost its:
options: Threshold population — the minimum customers it needs to survive

questions.question: The strips of open ground separating the township from the rest of the city in the South African model are:
options: Buffer strips drawn by apartheid planners

questions.question: Lwazi's long daily commute from the periphery to work near the core demonstrates:
options: That the apartheid city model deliberately placed homes far from workplaces
The low accessibility of the central business district

subtopics.title: How the Country Earns Its Keep

questions.question: In the household picture, the grandmother who grows and digs represents:
options: The primary sector — agriculture, fishing and mining

questions.question: The 'extension cord run to a neighbouring harbour' stands for:
options: An Industrial Development Zone such as Coega
A Spatial Development Initiative corridor such as the one to Maputo

questions.question: The vendor at the taxi rank and the backyard salon belong to:
options: The informal sector — unregistered and small-scale, but a vital survival net

questions.question: A gradient answer of 1:25 means:
options: You climb twenty-five metres for every metre walked
You climb one metre for every twenty-five metres of horizontal distance
The drawing is twenty-five times exaggerated

questions.question: Vertical exaggeration is calculated as:
options: Vertical scale divided by horizontal scale, answered as so-many times
Vertical interval divided by horizontal equivalent

questions.question: A distance answer written simply as '4' is unfinished because:
options: Distances must always be whole numbers
The unit of measurement must be stated in the final answer
Calculators are not permitted in mapwork
Distance answers must be given in centimetres only

questions.question: The evidence habit in map interpretation means:
options: Quoting the question back in the answer
Backing every claim with visible map evidence, like windpumps and cultivated land proving a rural settlement
